FingerFoniks1 — Help

Make speech and music with your fingers

FingerFoniks1 is a phoneme speech synthesizer. Phonemes are the individual sounds that make up words. Combine sounds on the colored grid to create speech, then use the piano keyboard to give those sounds a melody.

Play the phoneme grid

Touch a colored cell to hear its sound. Slide from cell to cell to join sounds together. Tap the phoneme cell again to silence it or let the Delay do it automatically. The four corner dots mark syllable boundaries and end the preceding sound. Stop consonants produce short sounds.

Turn on Pitch to bend a phoneme by sliding vertically within its cell: top is +2 semitones, middle is normal pitch, and bottom is −2 semitones. Return / Stay selects the release behavior. Return returns pitch to the middle when you lift your finger. Stay keeps the selected pitch after release and when touching another phoneme. Stay is selected initially. Turn Pitch off to return to normal pitch and disable bending.

Control the sound

Volume adjusts loudness. Brightness changes the tone. Transition controls how quickly one phoneme changes into another. Decay Length controls the fade after release. Hold a phoneme cell or piano key to sustain the sound, then lift your finger to begin the fade; stop consonants keep their short envelopes.

My Voice

The voice selector offers My recordings (My Voice) and DECtalk. My Voice plays your own recorded phonemes on the grid and in songs. Any phoneme you have not recorded still uses DECtalk, so you can begin with just a few recordings. Select DECtalk whenever you want the built-in voice for every phoneme. A small white dot on a grid cell indicates that it has a recording.

The piano keyboard changes the pitch of recorded sounds. Sustained sounds repeat a selected loop, while stop consonants and ch/j play once. Decay Length controls the fade of recorded sounds, just as it does with DECtalk; stop consonants keep their short envelopes. Changing playback pitch also changes the recorded voice’s tone.

Record Voice

Press Record Voice to open the recording screen. Choose Recording note: C4 (middle C) or C3 (one octave lower). Press Hear C4 or Hear C3, then match that note while recording voiced sounds. Choose a Phoneme; the example word identifies the sound to record. Press Record, allow microphone access if asked, then press Stop when finished. Hold sustained sounds steadily for 2–3 seconds without saying their letter names. For p, b, t, d, k, g, ch and j, record one short sound. Leave a little silence at the start and end. Recording stops automatically after 10 seconds.

Import Audio lets you choose an existing audio file instead of using the microphone. If recording is unavailable in HTML Editor, record the sound in Voice Memos and import it.

Use Trim start and Trim end to remove silence and unwanted sound. For sustained phonemes, set Loop start and Loop end inside a steady part of the recording. Loop controls are disabled for stops and ch/j because these play once. Preview Original plays the trimmed recording; Preview Loop at C4/C3 lets you check its sustained sound at the selected recording note. Stop Preview ends the preview.

Detect Pitch estimates the recorded pitch. Check the result with Preview Loop at the selected note and adjust Recorded pitch in Hz if needed. Hear C4/C3 plays the selected reference tone. Each saved phoneme keeps its own recorded pitch, so C4 and C3 recordings can be used together on the piano.

Press Use Recording to assign the recording and trim settings to the selected phoneme. This also selects My recordings. A check mark in the phoneme list identifies each assigned sound, and the count shows how many of the 31 phonemes are ready. Repeat for other phonemes as desired.

Save Voice to HTML creates a complete HTML app containing all your assigned recordings and the current trim changes. Use Copy HTML and save the document in HTML Editor, or use Try Download. Open the updated HTML next time to reuse your voice. The running app cannot overwrite the original HTML file automatically.

Export Voice Backup saves all assigned recordings and their trim, loop, and pitch settings in one voice backup file. Use the save interface to choose its name and location. Backups include the selected C3 or C4 recording note. Loading a backup shows its filename in the recording screen and main voice selector, and centers the piano on its saved recording note. Older backups use their recorded pitches to choose the octave. Load Voice Backup opens the file chooser to restore a saved voice bank and selects My Voice. After loading, use Save Voice to HTML if you want the restored voice included in a complete app file.

Done closes the recording screen. Use Recording applies your sound edits; Save Voice to HTML saves the app containing your recordings for reopening later.

Play a melody

Touch any piano key to play its exact note. Keep your finger down and slide to another key to glide smoothly to that note. When a song is loaded, each new key press plays the next syllable. Slide across keys to change the pitch of that syllable or slide vertically to produce tremelo; lift your finger before playing the next one.

Write and save songs

Select Write Song, then select phonemes and corner dots to build syllables. Use the phoneme line to review your sequence. Clear, Undo, and Redo help you edit it. The Tempo slider controls playback speed.

Tap Write Song to turn writing on or off. Turning it off keeps the current text and locks editing. While Write Song is active, type a song name in the Songs panel. Save to Files uses that name for the song file. After saving, Write Song turns off and the saved name and phonemes remain visible. Selecting Write Song again asks for confirmation before clearing the editor for a new song. Load from Files opens a saved song; its filename appears in the Songs panel.

Customize the grid

In Edit Layout, use Cell Position to swap cells and Cell Color to change their colors. Use Save and follow its instructions to keep your edited layout.

Press Close to return to the synthesizer.
